source.note: Battery 7 (anti-motor-torpedo-boat), Puffin Island. Photos by Curt Law and Joe Stevens, 22 Aug 1998 (kadiak.org).

k_puffin_puffin.caption: [Puffin Island. Page text: 'This was the WWII site of Battery 7 of the Kodiak Harbor Defenses, an anti motor torpedo boat battery'.]

k_puffin_map1.caption: Puffin Island map. Drawn from two others and field survey. The location of the 220 by 13 foot pier is approximate.

k_puffin_aug23_06.caption: Distant Electrical Control (DEC) bunker, structure No. 18. Kalsin Bay and Middle Bay in the background.
k_puffin_aug23_06.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_puffin_aug23_04.caption: Generator house, structure No. 7
k_puffin_aug23_04.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_puffin_aug23_05.caption: Recreation hall, structure No. 6
k_puffin_aug23_05.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_puffin_aug23_08.caption: EM barracks, structure No. 1. Gun emplacement is on the ridge beyond. All the little white dots are sea gulls.
k_puffin_aug23_08.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_puffin_aug23_10.caption: Covered ramp leading to underground battle allowance magazine, structure No. 14.
k_puffin_aug23_10.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_puffin_aug23_13.caption: There are two mounts for 90 milimeter guns. These were described as "anti-PT-boat" guns. Both mounts are east of the magazine. Two more guns were on mobile mounts. The pits are concrete and about four feet deep.
k_puffin_aug23_13.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_puffin_puffin13.caption: Small arms magazine, structure No. 15. Same construction as magazine, structure No. 16, not shown.
k_puffin_puffin13.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_puffin_puffin10.caption: Searchlight bunker No. 11. Lighting wiring still in place. No communications wiring found. This is very difficult to enter. It requires climbing down a steep, grassy, cliff with a fifty-foot drop-off to the surf and rocks below. The erosion around this bunker is severe.
k_puffin_puffin10.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)

k_puffin_puffin4.caption: Puffin Island from the south. The searchlight bunker, structure No. 17, also shown in photo 20 above, and the DEC bunker, structure No. 18, also shown in photos 6 and 15.
k_puffin_puffin4.credit: Photo: Curt Law, AL7LQ, and Joe Stevens, WL7AML, 22 August 1998 (via kadiak.org)
